page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. System memory totals 16.0 GB, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a local 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching a top-tier 36.47 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression single-threaded performance measured at a strong 15.05 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 4653.8 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 29.54 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only small block speed of 344.82 GB/sec and a large block speed of 43.94 GB/sec, though large block write bandwidth is weak at 23.77 GB/sec. Passmark metrics place the CPU score, database operations, and memory score in the average tier.

The hardware profile offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads, combining dedicated compute resources with high-speed local NVMe storage. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, provides acceleration for specific cryptographic and vector operations. Given the average multi-core scaling but strong single-core efficiency, this server is well-suited for applications that do not heavily saturate all cores simultaneously. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, which achieved 8.72 GB/sec in throughput tests, Redis caching, light database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.

It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs from 2 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores running at 4.2 GHz, supported by 16.0 GB of RAM and a local 236 GB NVMe SSD. Single-threaded performance is a key strength, with gzip compression reaching a top-tier 36.47 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression scoring a strong 15.05 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded CPU and write bandwidth benchmarks fall into the weaker tier. The instance features advanced CPU instructions like AVX-512 and AMX, making it highly capable for specialized vector and cryptographic tasks.
